comments.note: ThumbnailViewerViewModel.Thumbnails exposes IReadOnlyList<ThumbnailItemViewModel> rather than ObservableCollection — the viewer is read-only so ObservableCollection adds no value. The ledger AC spec says ObservableCollection but the WP spec (WP-012.md) says IReadOnlyList; IReadOnlyList was used as it is more appropriate for this use case.

The CloseCommand fires a CloseRequested event rather than calling IThumbnailViewerService.CloseAsync (as the ledger AC states). IThumbnailViewerService does not exist yet (WP-021) and the spec file WP-012.md explicitly specifies an event; the event-based approach is correct for this ViewModel.

comments.note: No functional issues found. All AC intents are met. The two documented deviations from AC text are justified: IReadOnlyList<ThumbnailItemViewModel> is correct for a read-only viewer (ObservableCollection adds no value); CloseRequested event is the correct MVVM pattern when IThumbnailViewerService (WP-021) does not yet exist.

Property name mismatch vs AC text: implementation exposes PositionLabel (not NavigationLabel) and CurrentIndex (not CenterIndex/CurrentThumbnail). These are naming choices only; behavior is identical. Downstream XAML bindings should use PositionLabel and CurrentIndex/Current. Flagged for Reviewer awareness.

NavigatePreviousCommand/NavigateNextCommand use CanExecute guards (CanNavigatePrev/CanNavigateNext) rather than clamping inside the execute body. This is strictly safer — commands are disabled at bounds rather than silently no-op.

Empty-list edge case: PositionLabel returns '0 / 0' and Current returns null when _thumbnails is empty. Null-safe UI bindings required. Command guards (CanNavigatePrev = CurrentIndex > 0, CanNavigateNext = CurrentIndex < Count - 1) correctly disable both commands for empty list.

Current property is null-safe; PositionLabel handles empty-list case with '0 / 0'.
Navigation guards (CanNavigatePrev/CanNavigateNext) disable commands at bounds rather than clamping in the execute body, which is stricter and correct.

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. CommunityToolkit.Mvvm source generator attributes ([ObservableProperty], [NotifyPropertyChangedFor], [NotifyCanExecuteChangedFor], [RelayCommand]) are used correctly. CanExecute guards are preferred over in-body clamping, which is strictly safer. Setting _currentIndex (backing field) in the constructor correctly avoids premature change notifications.

IReadOnlyList<ThumbnailItemViewModel> over ObservableCollection is correct for a read-only viewer. The viewer is handed a snapshot; it doesn't need to react to external list mutations. AC text says ObservableCollection but the plan spec and implementation both correctly use IReadOnlyList.

CloseRequested event over IThumbnailViewerService.CloseAsync is correct MVVM practice when the service does not yet exist (WP-021). The event decouples the ViewModel from a service boundary that crosses the App layer, which is the right pattern.

Minor improvement: the initialIndex constructor parameter has no bounds validation or clamping. If a caller passes an out-of-range value (negative or ≥ Count), Current returns null and CanNavigatePrev/CanNavigateNext will be in an unexpected state. A Math.Clamp(initialIndex, 0, Math.Max(0, thumbnails.Count - 1)) guard would prevent this. Not blocking as the expected callers always pass a valid index, but worth addressing proactively.

ThumbnailItemViewModel implements IDisposable (holds an Avalonia Bitmap). ThumbnailViewerViewModel does not implement IDisposable and does not dispose items in the list, which is intentional — the caller owns the lifecycle. This ownership contract should be documented on the constructor so future maintainers do not assume the viewer disposes its items.

[documentation-forward] AC text uses ObservableCollection, NavigationLabel, CurrentThumbnail, and CenterIndex but the implementation correctly uses IReadOnlyList, PositionLabel, Current, and CurrentIndex. The Documentation agent should update work/WP-018.md AC text to match the actual property names so future agents reading the WP are not confused by the discrepancy.

[documentation-forward] ThumbnailViewerViewModel constructor should carry a doc comment clarifying that the caller retains ownership of and is responsible for disposing the ThumbnailItemViewModel instances passed in the list.
